messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P0 -> Auriga (enterprise, VPC) — northstar region; affected: dedicated pool auriga-prod-1; symptoms: increased 5xx rate on model inference, higher token latency, some requests timing out. PD alert: 1998501234.
Erin: taking primary oncall. I'm on to triage. tagging @Maya @Rajiv.
Rajiv: on it — starting root cause checks for model serving nodes in auriga-prod-1. will confirm kernel / oom / queue backlog.
Maya: I see brief network flap in northstar-us-1 az1 around 08:03 UTC, nothing in peering but BGP flaps to the edge for that pool. Investigating.
Erin: quick impact summary for CS: looks like ~30% of tenant requests are hitting 5xx, customers in NA region (Auriga) are complaining. Carlos, can you stand by to notify the account?
Carlos: standby — I'll DM Cedric and prep a short note for the account. want to avoid alarm until we have mitigation.
Rajiv: backlog and CPU on the dedicated pool controller are high; KV cache misses spiking. looks like a slow IO issue on a subset of GPUs — starting a warm pool scale to move traffic.
Erin: plan: 1) scale up auriga-prod-warm in northstar-us-2 to required capacity (warm capacity already pre-provisioned but needs replicas). 2) shift customer traffic from auriga-prod-1 to auriga-prod-warm via DNS CNAME cutover + ingress weight change. 3) monitor health checks and gradual weight shift. 4) keep fallback route to global edge if problems.
Suzanne: +1 to that plan. add a low-TTL DNS window and a canary step at 10% for 5 minutes. I'll take on rollback steps if we need to revert.
Tom: I'll prep the edge routing change once warm pool reports healthy. I can change route weights in TrafficController: `tcctl route update --service auriga-enterprise --from auriga-prod-1:100 --to auriga-prod-warm:0` then increment.
Erin: Rajiv, can you run the warm scale now? paste commands and estimated time.
Rajiv: running: `./infra/scale-pool --pool auriga-prod-warm --region northstar-us-2 --replicas 12 --wait` ETA ~6m to reach steady. starting now.
deploy-bot: deployment/scale job started for auriga-prod-warm by Rajiv (job id d-1998501240).
Maya: I will pre-warm routes and update BGP if needed. Also lowering DNS TTL for the customer CNAME to 30s: `dnsctl set-ttl auriga.customer. -> 30s` — doing that now.
Erin: Carlos pls hold the customer message short: "We're shifting traffic to a warm pool to restore performance; minimal disruption expected; will update in 15 min."
Carlos: message sent to Cedric (CS). Cedric acknowledges and will watch incoming customer replies.
Rajiv: warm pool reached 12 replicas and health checks passing on model-serving pods. KV caches warming.
Erin: starting canary 10% traffic shift. Tom you good to update edge weights?
Tom: executing weight update: `tcctl route update --service auriga-enterprise --weights auriga-prod-1=90,auriga-prod-warm=10` — pushed.
Erin: monitoring logs and metrics. initial canary: 10% shows error rate drop to 8% from 30% on canary traffic. latency median down from 320ms to 120ms.
Suzanne: good signal. continue to 50% over next 3 minutes if stable. roll back threshold: if error rate on new pool >5% absolute or latency >200ms p95.
Erin: moving to 50%. Tom executing.
Tom: `tcctl route update --service auriga-enterprise --weights auriga-prod-1=50,auriga-prod-warm=50` — applied.
Rajiv: monitoring KV cold start errors; some legacy sessions failing due to cache keys missing — adding short-lived proxy fallback to fill in missing KV. Rolling config: `runtimectl proxy-enable --pool auriga-prod-warm --mode fill-missing`.
Erin: customers report latency improving, but one account (Cedric) saw 502s for a minute. Carlos, any signal from the account?
Carlos: Cedric says they saw brief 502 spikes but are okay; asked for ETA on full recovery. I told them we expect to finish shift in ~10m.
Maya: DNS TTL lowered successfully and CNAME update queued. since TTL 30s, full propagation within ~2m after final CNAME change.
Erin: moving to 90% now. Tom executing.
Tom: `tcctl route update --service auriga-enterprise --weights auriga-prod-1=10,auriga-prod-warm=90` — applied.
Erin: health checks stable, error rate on affected tenant down to 1.5%, latency within SLOs.
Rajiv: starting final cutover — change customer CNAME from `auriga.edge.example.net` -> `auriga-warm.edge.example.net`. `dnsctl upsert-cname auriga.customer. auriga-warm.edge.example.net`.
deploy-bot: dns change published (change id dc-1998501450).
Maya: verifying BGP and edge config for warm edge endpoints — all adjacencies stable.
Erin: full traffic now on warm pool; monitoring for residual errors. Carlos, letting account know full shift done and we are monitoring for 30m.
Carlos: message to Cedric sent: "We completed the traffic shift to a warm pool; things are stable now. We're monitoring for 30m and will follow up with a full incident note." Cedric replied thanks.
Suzanne: start incident timeline and assign postmortem. Owner: Rajiv for root cause, Erin for mitigation notes, Maya for network timeline, Carlos for customer comms. We should include runbook gaps: TTL handling and faster automatic warm shift.
Erin: handoff — Suzanne will be primary for next 30m while I step back (backup oncall). Suzanne: you good to take lead?
Suzanne: taking lead. Erin, thanks. I'll keep updates here and annotate timeline.
Erin: leaving notes in the incident doc: `https://redwood/incident/1998501234` — included commands executed, DNS change ids, and monitoring graphs.
Suzanne: adding follow-up actions: 1) detailed RCA, 2) add automated fallback that can switch ingress weights when controller CPU > 75% for 2m, 3) improve KV cache warm path.
Rajiv: initial suspect: intermittent IO at node-level causing slow GPU access and queue backpressure; collecting disk/driver logs and will attach to RCA.
Maya: adding network timeline: BGP jitter at 08:03 for ~90s for az1; likely contributed to control plane flakiness. Gathering router logs and will attach.
Tom: leaving commands used in thread for audits. happy to help with rollbacks if needed.
Suzanne: marking status: mitigated — traffic shifted to warm pool, customer impact minimal now. We'll keep thread open for monitoring and close after postmortem assignment and customer follow-up.
Carlos: customer acknowledged and will expect a postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident 1998501234 status: mitigated -> monitoring. paging channel will keep pinned.
Suzanne: last check in 20m, otherwise closing this thread at 1998501899 if stable.
Cedric: thanks team — appreciate the quick action.
Suzanne: noted. incident follow-up meeting scheduled for tomorrow 14:00 UTC.
